sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇāv atirathau hatau senāpatī mama senāpatir bhavān astu tābhyāṃ draviṇavattaraḥ
english: Bhīṣma and Droṇa, those peerless warriors, my two commanders, are slain. Let your good self be my commander, richer in might than both of them.

sanskrit: vṛddhau ca tau maheṣvāsau sāpekṣau ca dhanaṃjaye mānitau ca mayā vīrau rādheya vacanāt tava
english: Those two mighty archers were aged, and both bore tenderness toward Dhanaṃjaya; yet, O Rādheya, those heroes were honored by me at your word.

sanskrit: pitāmahatvaṃ saṃprekṣya pāṇḍuputrā mahāraṇe rakṣitās tāta bhīṣmeṇa divasāni daśaiva ha
english: Mindful of his grandsire's bond, dear one, Bhīṣma spared the sons of Pāṇḍu in the great battle for ten whole days.

sanskrit: nyastaśastre ca bhavati hato bhīṣmaḥ pitāmahaḥ śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya phalgunena mahāhave
english: And when his weapons were laid down, the grandsire Bhīṣma was slain in the great battle by Phalguna, who put Śikhaṇḍin to the fore.

sanskrit: hate tasmin mahābhāge śaratalpagate tadā tvayokte puruṣavyāghra droṇo hy āsīt puraḥsaraḥ
english: When that illustrious one fell and lay upon a bed of arrows, then, O tiger among men, at your word Droṇa became the foremost.

sanskrit: tenāpi rakṣitāḥ pārthāḥ śiṣyatvād iha saṃyuge sa cāpi nihato vṛddho dhṛṣṭadyumnena satvaram
english: He too spared the sons of Pṛthā in this combat, for they had been his pupils; and that aged one was swiftly slain by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: nihatābhyāṃ pradhānābhyāṃ tābhyām amitavikrama tvatsamaṃ samare yodhaṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmi cintayan
english: Now that those two chief warriors are slain, O man of measureless valor, however I ponder it, I see no other fighter in battle who is your equal.

sanskrit: bhavān eva tu naḥ śakto vijayāya na saṃśayaḥ pūrvaṃ madhye ca paścāc ca tavaiva viditaṃ hi tat
english: You alone are able to win us the victory, of this there is no doubt; before, in the midst, and after, all of this has been known to you indeed.

sanskrit: sa bhavān dhuryavat saṃkhye dhuram udvoḍhum arhasi abhiṣecaya senānye svayam ātmānam ātmanā
english: You, then, like a yoke-bearing steed, are worthy to bear the burden in battle; consecrate yourself by your own hand to the office of commander.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ yathā skandaḥ senānīḥ prabhur avyayaḥ tathā bhavān imāṃ senāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrīṃ bibhartu me jahi śatrugaṇān sarvān mahendra iva dānavān
english: As Skanda is the imperishable lord and commander of the gods, so let your good self sustain this army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son for me; strike down all the hosts of foes, as great Indra struck the Dānavas.

sanskrit: avasthitaṃ raṇe jñātvā pāṇḍavās tvāṃ mahāratham draviṣyanti sapāñcālā viṣṇuṃ dṛṣṭveva dānavāḥ tasmāt tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra prakarṣethā mahācamūm
english: When they learn that you, the great car-warrior, stand firm in battle, the Pāṇḍavas with the Pāñcālas will flee as the Dānavas fled at the sight of Viṣṇu; therefore, O tiger among men, lead forth the mighty host.

sanskrit: bhavaty avasthite yat te pāṇḍavā gatacetasaḥ bhaviṣyanti sahāmātyāḥ pāñcālaiḥ sṛñjayaiḥ saha
english: When you stand fast, the Pāṇḍavas, together with their counselors and with the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas, will be robbed of their senses.

sanskrit: yathā hy abhyuditaḥ sūryaḥ pratapan svena tejasā vyapohati tamas tīvraṃ tathā śatrūn vyapoha naḥ
english: For as the risen Sun, blazing with his own splendor, drives away the thick darkness, so do you drive away our foes.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca uktam etan mayā pūrvaṃ gāndhāre tava saṃnidhau jeṣyāmi pāṇḍavān rājan saputrān sajanārdanān
english: Karṇa said: This was spoken by me before, O son of Gāndhārī, in your presence: I shall conquer the Pāṇḍavas, O king, with their sons and with Janārdana.

sanskrit: senāpatir bhaviṣyāmi tavāhaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ sthiro bhava mahārāja jitān viddhi ca pāṇḍavān
english: I shall be your commander, herein there is no doubt; be steadfast, O great king, and know the Pāṇḍavas already vanquished.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam ukto mahātejās tato duryodhano nṛpaḥ uttasthau rājabhiḥ sārdhaṃ devair iva śatakratuḥ senāpatyena satkartuṃ karṇaṃ skandam ivāmarāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed, the mighty-spirited king Duryodhana then rose up together with the kings, like Indra of the hundred sacrifices amid the gods, to honor Karṇa with the command, as the immortals honored Skanda.

sanskrit: tato 'bhiṣiṣicus tūrṇaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā duryodhanamukhā rājan rājāno vijayaiṣiṇaḥ śātakaumbhamayaiḥ kumbhair māheyaiś cābhimantritaiḥ
english: Then swiftly, with rite ordained by scripture, the kings led by Duryodhana, O king, desiring victory, consecrated him with golden jars and with earthen ones over which the sacred mantras had been pronounced,

sanskrit: toyapūrṇair viṣāṇaiś ca dvīpikhaḍgamaharṣabhaiḥ maṇimuktāmayaiś cānyaiḥ puṇyagandhais tathauṣadhaiḥ
english: and with water-filled horns of leopards and rhinoceroses and great bulls, and with others made of gems and pearls, and with fragrant herbs of holy scent.

sanskrit: audumbare samāsīnam āsane kṣaumasaṃvṛtam śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā saṃbhāraiś ca susaṃbhṛtaiḥ
english: He was seated upon a throne of fig-wood draped with linen, consecrated by the rite seen in the scriptures and with the requisites well assembled.

sanskrit: jaya pārthān sagovindān sānugāṃs tvaṃ mahāhave iti taṃ bandinaḥ prāhur dvijāś ca bharatarṣabha
english: "Conquer the sons of Pṛthā, with Govinda and their followers, in the great battle!" Thus, O bull of the Bhāratas, the bards and the twice-born addressed him.

sanskrit: jahi pārthān sapāñcālān rādheya vijayāya naḥ udyann iva sadā bhānus tamāṃsy ugrair gabhastibhiḥ
english: "Strike down the sons of Pṛthā with the Pāñcālas, O Rādheya, for our victory, as the ever-rising Sun strikes the darkness with his fierce rays!"

sanskrit: na hy alaṃ tvad visṛṣṭānāṃ śarāṇāṃ te sakeśavāḥ kṛtaghnāḥ sūryaraśmīnāṃ jvalatām iva darśane
english: "For they, with Keśava, are no more a match for the arrows loosed by you than the ungrateful are for the gaze of the blazing rays of the Sun."

sanskrit: na hi pārthāḥ sapāñcālāḥ sthātuṃ śaktās tavāgrataḥ āttaśastrasya samare mahendrasyeva dānavāḥ
english: "For the sons of Pṛthā with the Pāñcālas can no more stand before you, weapon in hand in battle, than the Dānavas before great Indra."

sanskrit: abhiṣiktas tu rādheyaḥ prabhayā so 'mitaprabhaḥ vyatyaricyata rūpeṇa divākara ivāparaḥ
english: Consecrated, Rādheya of boundless radiance overflowed in his splendor of form, like a second maker of the day.

sanskrit: senāpatyena rādheyam abhiṣicya sutas tava amanyata tadātmānaṃ kṛtārthaṃ kālacoditaḥ
english: Having consecrated Rādheya to the command, your son, driven on by fate, then deemed his purpose accomplished.

sanskrit: karṇo 'pi rājan saṃprāpya senāpatyam ariṃdamaḥ yogam ājñāpayām āsa sūryasyodayanaṃ prati
english: And Karṇa too, O king, that subduer of foes, having gained the command, ordered the army to make ready against the rising of the Sun.

sanskrit: tava putrair vṛtaḥ karṇaḥ śuśubhe tatra bhārata devair iva yathā skandaḥ saṃgrāme tārakāmaye
english: Surrounded by your sons, Karṇa shone there, O Bhārata, as Skanda shone amid the gods in the war against Tāraka.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca senāpatyaṃ tu saṃprāpya karṇo vaikartanas tadā tathoktaś ca svayaṃ rājñā snigdhaṃ bhrātṛsamaṃ vacaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When Karṇa Vaikartana had gained the command and was thus addressed by the king himself with tender words, as to a brother,

sanskrit: yogam ājñāpya senāyā āditye 'bhyudite tadā akarot kiṃ mahāprājñas tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: having ordered the army to make ready when the Sun had risen, what did that man of great wisdom do? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca karṇasya matam ājñāya putras te bharatarṣabha yogam ājñāpayām āsa nāndītūryapuraḥsaram
english: Saṃjaya said: Learning Karṇa's purpose, O bull of the Bhāratas, your son ordered the array to be made ready, heralded by auspicious music.

sanskrit: mahaty apararātre tu tava putrasya māriṣa yogo yogeti sahasā prādurāsīn mahāsvanaḥ
english: In the great hours before dawn, O honored one, there arose all at once in your son's host a mighty din: "To arms! To arms!"

sanskrit: nāgānāṃ kalpamānānāṃ rathānāṃ ca varūthinām saṃnahyatāṃ padātīnāṃ vājināṃ ca viśāṃ pate
english: As the elephants were being harnessed and the guarded chariots made ready, as the foot-soldiers and the horses were being armed, O lord of peoples,

sanskrit: krośatāṃ cāpi yodhānāṃ tvaritānāṃ parasparam babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo divaspṛk sumahāṃs tadā
english: and as the warriors hurried, shouting to one another, there rose then a tumultuous uproar, vast and reaching the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ śvetapatākena bālārkākāravājinā hemapṛṣṭhena dhanuṣā hastikakṣyeṇa ketunā
english: Then with a white banner, with horses of the hue of the morning sun, with a gold-backed bow, with the elephant-girth ensign,

sanskrit: tūṇena śarapūrṇena sāṅgadena varūthinā śataghnīkiṅkiṇīśaktiśūlatomaradhāriṇā
english: with a quiver full of arrows, with an arm-band, guarded all round, bearing the hundred-slayer engines, bells, javelins, lances, and pikes,

sanskrit: kārmukeṇopapannena vimalādityavarcasā rathenātipatākena sūtaputro vyadṛśyata
english: furnished with a bow, with the radiance of the spotless sun, upon his tall-bannered chariot, the son of the charioteer appeared.

sanskrit: dhamantaṃ vārijaṃ tāta hemajālavibhūṣitam vidhunvānaṃ mahac cāpaṃ kārtasvaravibhūṣitam
english: He was blowing his conch, dear one, adorned with a net of gold, and brandishing his great bow decked with gold.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ rathasthaṃ rathināṃ varam bhānumantam ivodyantaṃ tamo ghnantaṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: Seeing Karṇa, the great archer, the foremost of car-warriors, standing on his chariot like the rising Sun dispelling the darkness a thousandfold—

sanskrit: na bhīṣmavyasanaṃ ke cin nāpi droṇasya māriṣa nānyeṣāṃ puruṣavyāghra menire tatra kauravāḥ
english: none of the Kauravas there, O honored one, then took to heart the calamity of Bhīṣma, nor of Droṇa, nor of the others, O tiger among men.

sanskrit: tatas tu tvarayan yodhāñ śaṅkhaśabdena māriṣa karṇo niṣkāsayām āsa kauravāṇāṃ varūthinīm
english: Then, urging on the warriors with the blast of his conch, O honored one, Karṇa led forth the host of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: vyūhaṃ vyūhya maheṣvāso mākaraṃ śatrutāpanaḥ pratyudyayau tadā karṇaḥ pāṇḍavān vijigīṣayā
english: Having arrayed his troops in the crocodile-formation, the great archer Karṇa, scorcher of foes, then advanced against the Pāṇḍavas, longing for victory.

sanskrit: makarasya tu tuṇḍe vai karṇo rājan vyavasthitaḥ netrābhyāṃ śakuniḥ śūra ulūkaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: At the snout of the crocodile Karṇa took his stand, O king; at its two eyes were the brave Śakuni and Ulūka, the great car-warrior.

sanskrit: droṇaputras tu śirasi grīvāyāṃ sarvasodarāḥ madhye duryodhano rājā balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
english: At the head was the son of Droṇa; at the neck were all your full brothers; in the center stood King Duryodhana, encircled by a mighty force.

sanskrit: vāme pāde tu rājendra kṛtavarmā vyavasthitaḥ nārāyaṇabalair yukto gopālair yuddhadurmadaḥ
english: At the left foot, O lord of kings, stood Kṛtavarman, joined with the Nārāyaṇa hosts, the cowherds, hard to vanquish in war.

sanskrit: pāde tu dakṣiṇe rājan gautamaḥ satyavikramaḥ trigartaiś ca maheṣvāsair dākṣiṇātyaiś ca saṃvṛtaḥ
english: At the right foot, O king, was Gautama of true valor, surrounded by the Trigartas, great archers, and by the men of the south.

sanskrit: anupādas tu yo vāmas tatra śalyo vyavasthitaḥ mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ madradeśasamutthayā
english: At the left hindfoot stood Śalya, together with a great army raised from the land of the Madras.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇe tu mahārāja suṣeṇaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ vṛto rathasahasraiś ca dantināṃ ca śatais tathā
english: At the right, O great king, was Suṣeṇa, true to his pledge, encircled by thousands of chariots and by hundreds of tusked elephants.

sanskrit: pucche āstāṃ mahāvīrau bhrātarau pārthivau tadā citrasenaś ca citraś ca mahatyā senayā vṛtau
english: At the tail stood the two great heroes, the royal brothers, Citrasena and Citra, encircled by a mighty army.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayāte rājendra karṇe naravarottame dhanaṃjayam abhiprekṣya dharmarājo 'bravīd idam
english: Then, when Karṇa, the best of warriors, had set forth, O lord of kings, the King of Righteousness looked upon Dhanaṃjaya and said this:

sanskrit: paśya pārtha mahāsenāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya saṃyuge karṇena nirmitāṃ vīra guptāṃ vīrair mahārathaiḥ
english: "Behold, O Pārtha, the great army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son in the battle, arrayed by Karṇa, O hero, and guarded by heroic car-warriors."

sanskrit: hatavīratamā hy eṣā dhārtarāṣṭrī mahācamūḥ phalguśeṣā mahābāho tṛṇais tulyā matā mama
english: "Robbed of its bravest, this great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, with but its dregs remaining, O mighty-armed one, I deem no better than straw."

sanskrit: eko hy atra maheṣvāsaḥ sūtaputro vyavasthitaḥ sadevāsuragandharvaiḥ sakiṃnaramahoragaiḥ carācarais tribhir lokair yo 'jayyo rathināṃ varaḥ
english: "One great archer alone stands firm here, the son of the charioteer, the best of car-warriors, who is unconquerable by the three worlds, moving and unmoving, with their gods, demons, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and great serpents."

sanskrit: taṃ hatvādya mahābāho vijayas tava phalguna uddhṛtaś ca bhavec chalyo mama dvādaśavārṣikaḥ evaṃ jñātvā mahābāho vyūhaṃ vyūha yathecchasi
english: "Slaying him today, O mighty-armed Phalguna, victory shall be yours, and the thorn of twelve years' standing shall be plucked from me; knowing this, O mighty-armed one, array the troops as you wish."

sanskrit: bhrātus tad vacanaṃ śrutvā pāṇḍavaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ ardhacandreṇa vyūhena pratyavyūhata tāṃ camūm
english: Hearing his brother's words, the white-horsed son of Pāṇḍu countered that host with a half-moon formation.

sanskrit: vāmapārśve 'bhavad rājan bhīmaseno vyavasthitaḥ dakṣiṇe ca maheṣvāso dhṛṣṭadyumno mahābalaḥ
english: On the left flank, O king, Bhīmasena took his stand, and on the right the great archer Dhṛṣṭadyumna of mighty strength.

sanskrit: madhye vyūhasya sākṣāt tu pāṇḍavaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dharmarājaś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: In the very center of the array stood the son of Pāṇḍu with Kṛṣṇa for his charioteer; behind him were Nakula and Sahadeva and the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣau tu pāñcālyau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau nārjunaṃ jahatur yuddhe pālyamānau kirīṭinā
english: The two Pāñcālas, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, his wheel-guards, did not forsake Arjuna in battle, themselves protected by the Diademed One.

sanskrit: śeṣā nṛpatayo vīrāḥ sthitā vyūhasya daṃśitāḥ yathābhāvaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yathāsattvaṃ ca bhārata
english: The remaining heroic kings, mailed, took their places in the array, each according to his rank, his ardor, and his strength, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evam etan mahāvyūhaṃ vyūhya bhārata pāṇḍavāḥ tāvakāś ca maheṣvāsā yuddhāyaiva mano dadhuḥ
english: Having thus arrayed that great formation, O Bhārata, the Pāṇḍavas and your own great archers set their minds upon battle alone.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vyūḍhāṃ tava camūṃ sūtaputreṇa saṃyuge nihatān pāṇḍavān mene tava putraḥ sahānvayaḥ
english: Seeing your host arrayed for battle by the son of the charioteer, your son, with his kinsmen, deemed the Pāṇḍavas already slain.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ vyūḍhāṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dhārtarāṣṭrān hatān mene sakarṇān vai janādhipa
english: And likewise, seeing the Pāṇḍava army arrayed, Yudhiṣṭhira deemed the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with Karṇa, already slain, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ sahasaivābhyahanyanta saśabdāś ca samantataḥ
english: Then the conches and kettledrums, the tabors, drums, and cow-horns were all at once sounded together, resounding on every side.

sanskrit: senayor ubhayo rājan prāvādyanta mahāsvanāḥ siṃhanādaś ca saṃjajñe śūrāṇāṃ jayagṛddhinām
english: In both armies, O king, the great-voiced instruments rang out, and the lion-roar of the heroes greedy for victory arose.

sanskrit: hayaheṣitaśabdāś ca vāraṇānāṃ ca bṛṃhitam rathanemisvanāś cogrāḥ saṃbabhūvur janādhipa
english: The neighing of horses, the trumpeting of elephants, and the fierce rumble of chariot-wheels arose, O lord of men.

sanskrit: na droṇavyasanaṃ kaś cij jānīte bharatarṣabha dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ mukhe vyūhasya daṃśitam
english: No one took to heart the calamity of Droṇa, O bull of the Bhāratas, on seeing the great archer Karṇa, mailed, at the front of the array.

sanskrit: ubhe sene mahāsattve prahṛṣṭanarakuñjare yoddhukāme sthite rājan hantum anyonyam añjasā
english: Both armies, of great might, with men and elephants exultant, eager to fight, stood ready, O king, to slay one another at once.

sanskrit: tatra yattau susaṃrabdhau dṛṣṭvānyonyaṃ vyavasthitau anīkamadhye rājendra rejatuḥ karṇapāṇḍavau
english: There, intent and inflamed with wrath, having beheld each other take their stand in the midst of the hosts, Karṇa and the son of Pāṇḍu shone forth, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: nṛtyamāne tu te sene sameyātāṃ parasparam tayoḥ pakṣaiḥ prapakṣaiś ca nirjagmur vai yuyutsavaḥ
english: As the two armies seemed to dance, they came together against each other; and from their wings and from the wings beyond the wings the eager combatants sallied forth.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ naravāraṇavājinām rathināṃ ca mahārāja anyonyaṃ nighnatāṃ dṛḍham
english: Then began the battle of men, elephants, and horses, and of car-warriors, O great king, smiting one another fiercely.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca te sene 'nyonyam āsādya prahṛṣṭāśvanaradvipe bṛhatyau saṃprajahrāte devāsuracamūpame
english: Saṃjaya said: Those two armies, vast, with horses, men, and elephants exultant, closing upon each other, fell to blows, like the hosts of gods and demons.

sanskrit: tato gajā rathāś cāśvāḥ pattayaś ca mahāhave saṃprahāraṃ paraṃ cakrur dehapāpmapraṇāśanam
english: Then elephants, chariots, horses, and foot-soldiers in the great battle dealt one another a supreme onslaught that made an end of body and of sin.

sanskrit: pūrṇacandrārkapadmānāṃ kāntitviḍgandhataḥ samaiḥ uttamāṅgair nṛsiṃhānāṃ nṛsiṃhās tastarur mahīm
english: With the severed heads of lions among men—heads matching in loveliness, luster, and fragrance the full moon, the sun, and the lotus—the lions among men strewed the earth.

sanskrit: ardhacandrais tathā bhallaiḥ kṣuraprair asipaṭṭiśaiḥ paraśvadhaiś cāpy akṛntann uttamāṅgāni yudhyatām
english: With crescent-headed shafts, with broad arrows, with razor-tipped darts, with swords and spears, and with battle-axes, they cut off the heads of those who fought.

sanskrit: vyāyatāyatabāhūnāṃ vyāyatāyatabāhubhiḥ vyāyatā bāhavaḥ petuś chinnamuṣṭyāyudhāṅgadāḥ
english: By the long, outstretched arms of warriors with long, outstretched arms, the long arms of others were made to fall, their fists, weapons, and arm-bands severed.

sanskrit: taiḥ sphuradbhir mahī bhāti raktāṅgulitalais tadā garuḍaprahatair ugraiḥ pañcāsyair iva pannagaiḥ
english: The earth then gleamed with those quivering arms, their fingers and palms blood-red, like fierce five-hooded serpents struck down by Garuḍa.

sanskrit: hayasyandananāgebhyaḥ petur vīrā dviṣaddhatāḥ vimānebhyo yathā kṣīṇe puṇye svargasadas tathā
english: From horses, chariots, and elephants the heroes, slain by their foes, fell as the dwellers in heaven fall from their celestial cars when their merit is spent.

sanskrit: gadābhir anyair gurvībhiḥ parighair musalair api pothitāḥ śataśaḥ petur vīrā vīratarai raṇe
english: Crushed by heavy maces, by iron bludgeons and by pestles, the heroes fell by the hundreds, struck down by braver heroes in the battle.

sanskrit: rathā rathair vinihatā mattā mattair dvipair dvipāḥ sādinaḥ sādibhiś caiva tasmin paramasaṃkule
english: Chariots were destroyed by chariots, frenzied elephants by frenzied elephants, and horsemen by horsemen, in that utmost tumult.

sanskrit: rathā vararathair nāgair aśvārohāś ca pattibhiḥ aśvārohaiḥ padātāś ca nihatā yudhi śerate
english: Chariots slain by noble chariots and by elephants, and horsemen by foot-soldiers, and foot-soldiers by horsemen, lay outstretched, slain in the fight.

sanskrit: rathāśvapattayo nāgai rathair nāgāś ca pattayaḥ rathapattidvipāś cāśvair nṛbhiś cāśvarathadvipāḥ
english: Chariots, horses, and foot-soldiers were slain by elephants, and elephants and foot-soldiers by chariots; chariots, foot-soldiers, and elephants by horses, and horses, chariots, and elephants by men.
